Select interaction effects

Source: vignettes/articles/interactions.Rmd
interactions.Rmd

Interaction effects describe how one predictor’s association with the response depends on another predictor. L0glm can generate these terms after selecting the main effects, then repeat sparse selection on the expanded candidate set. This keeps the working design manageable when there are many original predictors.

Fit a model with interaction effects

interactions controls the stages of interaction generation:

Setting Candidate terms
0L Main effects
1L Main effects and pairwise products
2L Also three-way products

The default is 0L. The following example includes signed main effects, a pairwise interaction and a three-way interaction.

library(L0glm)
set.seed(171)
X <- matrix(rnorm(300*12),300,12,dimnames=list(NULL,letters[1:12]))
y <- 1+2*X[,1]-2*X[,2]+2*X[,3]+2*X[,1]*X[,2]+
  2*X[,1]*X[,2]*X[,3]+rnorm(300)
fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,family=gaussian(),intercept=TRUE,lambda='gic',
  interactions=2L,relaxed=TRUE,dispersion=1)
fit$interactions$history
#>   order   lambda df     score selected
#> 1     0 4.326544  7 2314.4139    FALSE
#> 2     1 5.738479 11 1497.0640    FALSE
#> 3     2 5.801800  7  891.4203     TRUE
coef(fit)[which(Matrix::rowSums(coef(fit)!=0)>0),,drop=FALSE]
#> 7 x 1 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>                     
#> Intercept  1.1308508
#> a          1.9366800
#> b         -2.0177199
#> c          1.9709521
#> a:b        2.0485638
#> c:k       -0.1631733
#> a:b:c      2.0009853

Only selected original main effects generate products. The two-way stage forms pairwise products, and the next stage forms three-way products among the original main effects still selected. Each predictor appears once per product. Intercepts and compulsory terms remain main effects. All generated terms stay available in subsequent stages, and subsequent selection can discard a parent main effect.

For named presets, the penalty is recalculated from the original selectable predictor count plus the generated products. Stage scores use a common final candidate count and the usual free-coefficient degrees of freedom. The best stage is retained. A numeric lambda remains fixed across stages.

Prediction and reproducibility

Prediction accepts the original main-effect columns and creates the products it needs. Sparse inputs retain sparse storage. The model keeps a lightweight training-design view, avoiding a second copy of all original columns.

predict(fit,X[1:5,])
#>            [,1]
#> [1,] -0.3918658
#> [2,]  5.0938261
#> [3,]  2.0842669
#> [4,] -2.8144644
#> [5,]  4.3704328
fit$interactions$terms

The recipe includes the fitting specification, so the complete pipeline can be repeated with the original data:

repeated <- do.call(l0glmFit,c(list(X=X,y=y),fit$interactions$specification))

Explicit starting-zero exclusions also constrain products in the corresponding response channel. New products receive normalized-coordinate starts and prior mean zero. Predictor groups are supported; products with the same tuple of parent group labels form an interaction group.

Cross-validation and validation stopping 

cv <- l0glmTune(X,y,family=gaussian(),intercept=TRUE,interactions=2L,
  tune='cv',nfolds=5L,nlambda=10L,relaxed=TRUE)
predict(cv$fit_1se,X[1:5,])

Every training fold selects its own main effects and generates its own products. Full-data paths share a union of product rows for plotting, with zeros for terms absent from a fit. Independent validation data can also choose the best stage: pass validation=list(X=V,y=v), using the original main-effect columns. Generation stops when validation deviance worsens.

control.interactions bounds the candidate count and working-design size before products are constructed. See interaction models for the mathematical convention, controls and returned recipe.
